Bengaluru accounts for more than half of recipients, with 24.05 lakh voters across its four electoral districts set to receive notices. Of these, 20.35 lakh voters have been flagged for “logical discrepancies” in their enumeration forms, while 23.45 lakh could not provide mapping details from the 2002 electoral roll. The notices will be issued after draft electoral rolls are published on August 24. The claims and objections period will continue until September 23, while their disposal will continue until October 22. The Chief Electoral Officer’s office has identified nine categories of logical discrepancies. These include implausible age gaps between parents and children, discrepancies in fathers’ names and differences between current and previous electoral records. Other categories include age gaps between siblings, unusually high numbers of children mapped to a parent, and discrepancies in voters’ own names between the current roll and the previous SIR.
